source.publication: Instructions for 2025 PIT-ADJ; 2025 PIT-1 Personal Income Tax Return Instructions; 2025 Tax Rate Table (Tax Look Up Table)
source.section: PIT-ADJ instructions PDF page 3, line 10; Form PIT-1 lines 9 to 18 and 22; instructions PDF page 25, line 12; Tax Rate Table PDF pages 1 to 6, rows; PDF page 7 (T-7), over 100,000

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (person 1) 40,000.00 + IRA distribution (person 1) 30,000.00 + Railroad Retirement benefits (person 0) 60,000.00 = 130,000.00. Federal taxable income = 130,000.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 - 2 x 1,600.00 additional for age 65 or older = 95,300.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; Form PIT-1 takes only the federal line 12 amount, and no line for what the federal return subtracts after line 12). Form PIT-1, married filing jointly. Line 9 federal AGI 130,000.00. Line 10 0.00 (standard deduction taken). Line 11 additions 0.00. Line 12 federal standard deduction 34,700.00. Line 13 dependents 0.00. Line 14 0.00: federal AGI 130,000.00 is over the worksheet's printed ceiling 55,000.00 for this status, so the worksheet is not completed. Line 15, PIT-ADJ: line 13 age 65 or older: Table 1 (married filing jointly) row for federal AGI 130,000.00 gives 0.00 x 2 qualifying = 0.00; line 10 Railroad Retirement benefits, exempt in full = 60,000.00; PIT-ADJ line 28 total 60,000.00. Line 17 = 130,000.00 + 0.00 - 34,700.00 - 0.00 - 60,000.00 = 35,300.00. By the projection: state_agi = federal taxable income 95,300.00 - 60,000.00 = 35,300.00; less base deductions 0.00 gives 35,300.00. Line 18 tax, schedule as numbers: 1.5% x 8,000.00 = 120 + 3.2% x 17,000.00 = 544 + 4.3% x 10,300.00 = 442.9; total 1,106.9, to the cent 1,106.90. The table row over 35,200 to 35,300 gives 1,105; expected keeps the formula figure. Lines 19 to 21 0.00. Line 22 net New Mexico income tax 1,106.90. No cap: the whole 60,000.00 is exempt.
